assignments.reason: The pidyon (redemption) and hamtaka (sweetening) is the comprehensive redemptive act that encompasses all 24 courts of judgment. The Torah explicitly identifies this as Moses' essential work: 'כָּל עֲבוֹדַת מֹשֶׁה – לְהַמְתִּיק' — Moses' entire service IS the sweetening. The pidyon's essential nature is not the divine-favor channel it requires (that is Package 1, eit ratzon), nor the evil domain it transforms (Package 3), but the mediating act itself — which is the defining function of Moses as the one who stands between shemad and ratzon. The pidyon IS the operational expression of Moses' cosmic mediating identity.

Converts (gerim) are the purpose and product of Moses' entire mission. The Torah states: 'כָּל עֲבוֹדַת מֹשֶׁה בְּחַיָּיו, וְעַכְשָׁו לְאַחַר מוֹתוֹ, הוּא רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת גֵּרִים' — Moses' entire work, in life and after death, is solely to make converts. The essential nature of gerim in this Torah is inextricable from Moses' identity as mediator: they are the living proof of the transformation from shemad (destruction/idolatry) to ratzon (divine will). Jethro converted because he was Moses' father-in-law; Rabbi Eliezer made converts because he was a reincarnation of Moses' son. Gerim belong to Moses' package by essential nature, not merely by causal connection.

This node describes the act of sweetening judgment and wrath — 'when they sweeten the din and the charon af.' While the objects being sweetened (din, charon af) belong to the evil domain (Package 3), the essential nature of this node is the sweetening process itself, which is the holy, redemptive act that defines Moses' cosmic function. The Rebbe says Moses 'stands always to sweeten the shemad and turn it to ratzon' — this node is that very act of standing-and-sweetening. Its essential nature is the mediating action, placing it in Moses' package. Polarity is good because sweetening is a positive, holy transformation.

This node describes the completed transformation: 'the idol worshippers are sweetened and become converts.' Although it references the akum (Package 3's evil domain), its essential nature is the realized outcome of Moses' mediation — the successful conversion of shemad into ratzon. The node captures the moment of transformation, not the evil state being transformed. The akum are no longer akum in this node; they have become gerim. This places the node's essential nature in the domain of Moses' redemptive mission (Package 2), on the ratzon side of his mediating identity. Polarity is good because the transformation is complete and the result is holy.
